stories.headline: FOMC begins two-day meeting; press-reported hold odds ease to 64-66% ahead of Wednesday's decision
stories.one_line: FOMC meeting begins today (Day 1 of 2); press-reported CME-style odds as of Monday's close eased to ~64-66% hold / 34-36% hike, down modestly from 33-39% hike odds last week, tracking the oil-price reversal since the ceasefire. This run's own FRED pull shows June CPI essentially flat MoM (-0.42%) and a soft +57k payrolls print alongside unemployment ticking down to 4.2% -- a genuinely mixed data backdrop. Today: $44B 7-Year and $95B 6-Week Bill auctions, 1pm ET.
stories.score_note: Highest-importance scheduled event of the week; drives rates and equities broadly.

stories.headline: Earnings week opens: Boeing wider loss on revenue beat/record backlog; Royal Caribbean and Coca-Cola beat and raise guidance
stories.one_line: Boeing Q2: revenue $24.6B (+8% YoY, beat), GAAP loss ($0.67)/share vs ~($0.31) consensus (wider than expected), record $715B backlog. Royal Caribbean: EPS $4.20/$4.21 adj (beat $4.02 est), raised FY guidance to $17.73-$17.87, flagged 'modest booking impact...due to prolonged geopolitical activity.' Coca-Cola: adj EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 est, raised FY guidance. Ford reports after close today; Microsoft/Meta/Arm/Qualcomm/SoFi Wed, Apple/Amazon/XOM/CVX/others Thu.
stories.score_note: Concentrated index-level risk given combined mega-cap weight; lands same week as FOMC.

stories.headline: AI-capex financing anxiety spreads to Asia: Samsung/SK Hynix post worst sessions in ~2 decades
stories.one_line: Samsung -13.4%, SK Hynix -14.7% (worst in ~2 decades), KOSPI -730pts overnight, reported to reflect concern that the Nvidia/OpenAI financing report signals AI-infra fragility, compounded by CXMT competitiveness reports. US premarket: NQ futures -2.6% (this run's own Yahoo pull) vs YM futures +1.6% -- a rotation, not broad risk-off. No company (Nvidia/OpenAI/SoftBank/Samsung/SK Hynix) has directly confirmed the causal link.
stories.score_note: Largest cross-border market mover this week; raises AI-capex vendor-financing circularity question ahead of Wed/Thu hyperscaler earnings.
sources: this run's own Yahoo Finance futures pull (primary)

stories.headline: US-Iran pause holds a fifth day; Trump and Iran give contradictory public accounts of diplomatic track
stories.one_line: No new strikes. Trump said US halted strikes 'at Iran's request,' expects a deal; an Iranian FM spokesperson said 'no negotiations...at present' -- first public sign of a messaging gap. Trump hosting Netanyahu and Zelenskyy separately in DC today, tied to Sen. Lindsey Graham's funeral; Netanyahu says Iran is 'first and foremost' on the agenda.
stories.score_note: High-risk/war-adjacent story with direct market impact; two-source rule applied.

stories.headline: Iran vows retaliation against Ukraine over Caspian Sea strike; Israel-provocation claim remains unevidenced
stories.one_line: No new strike or retaliatory action since Sunday. Araghchi's unevidenced accusation that Israel provoked the strike 'at Israel's behest' stands, unresponded to by Israel or Ukraine; the Iranian lawmaker's retaliation warning against Ukraine remains unacted upon three days on.
stories.score_note: Escalation risk for the broader Iran conflict, now entangled with Russia-Ukraine; watch for Iranian action.

stories.headline: Magnitude-7.1 earthquake strikes Kumamoto, Japan; tsunami advisory lifted, mall partial-collapse under review
stories.one_line: JMA M7.1 / USGS M6.8, Kumamoto Prefecture, Kyushu, 16:27 JST (03:27 ET). 50+ injured, ~12 houses collapsed, 48,300 households lost power, JR Kyushu bullet-train suspended, Kyushu Expressway sections shifted, Aeon Kashima mall partially collapsed with people reportedly trapped (cause unconfirmed). Tsunami advisory (up to 1m) issued and lifted within ~2 hours. No Kyushu chip/electronics facility damage disclosed yet.
stories.score_note: Active disaster story with real infrastructure disruption in a major chip-manufacturing region; forecast 2026-07-28-am-3 tracks facility-damage disclosure.

stories.headline: DOJ asks Supreme Court to stay injunction blocking mail-ballot executive order in 23 states
stories.one_line: 1st Circuit upheld a district-court injunction (Judge Talwani) blocking the EO in 23 states + DC Jul 25; DOJ filed an emergency SCOTUS stay application Monday. EO directs federal agencies to help build eligible-voter lists, USPS to deliver mail ballots only to listed voters, DOJ to prioritize investigations of officials issuing ballots to ineligible voters. States must respond by Aug 3.
stories.score_note: Live emergency Supreme Court matter with a stated response deadline; first tracked this run.

stories.headline: Q2 2026 GDP advance estimate, Thu Jul 30 8:30 ET
stories.one_line: No new information found this run; forecast 2026-07-27-am-2 (1.0-2.5% range) stands.
stories.score_note: Critical scheduled macro release, one day after FOMC.

stories.headline: Employment Cost Index Q2 2026, Fri Jul 31 8:30 ET
stories.one_line: Fed's preferred wage-inflation gauge, closes out the week's data calendar. No new information this run.

stories.headline: SpaceX confirms Starship booster landing-burn engines didn't all relight; SPCX at new low ahead of Aug 6 lockup
stories.one_line: SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot confirmed on-record that not all 13 planned landing-burn engines lit, targeting a softer splashdown -- upgrades the prior telemetry-inferred 10->8->5 engine count from inference to company confirmation. Deutsche Bank called the flight 'solid progress' despite the setback. SPCX hit a new intraday low ($109.53) before closing -1.36% at $113.50 (this run's own Twelve Data pull); Aug 6 lockup expiration (up to 911.5M shares, ~1.4x float) cited as a bigger driver of the muted reaction than flight performance.
stories.score_note: Backdrop/context item for public-company technical track record; SPCX float dynamics ahead of Aug 6 worth watching.
sources: this run's own Twelve Data pull (primary)

stories.headline: Fairlife resumes majority production; Anubis leak/payment still unresolved; Cl0p/ShinyHunters unchanged
stories.one_line: Coca-Cola says Fairlife has 'resumed the majority of production' at all four US plants after the Anubis ransomware attack; no leak-site posting or ransom payment confirmed (forecast 2026-07-27-pm-1, 45-60% by Jul 30, still open). Cl0p/PTC Windchill (CVE-2026-12569) mass-email extortion continues, no leak-site listing yet. ShinyHunters/EY deadline Jul 31, unchanged.
stories.score_note: Background single-name/reputational risk; production-restart is a genuine operational recovery signal.

stories.headline: Origin Energy (Australia) confirms ~900,000-customer breach; Arista VeloCloud zero-day added to CISA KEV
stories.one_line: Origin Energy: initial forensic review found ~900,000 current/former customers' data accessed (names, addresses, DOB, phone, account info, partial card/bank digits); breach confirmed ~Jul 22, notifications underway. Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator: CVSS-10.0 zero-day (CVE-2026-16812) under active exploitation, fixes shipped, added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a Jul 30 federal patch deadline. No attacker attribution reported for either.
stories.score_note: New incidents this run, unrelated to each other; grouped for the day's cyber roundup.

stories.headline: OpenAI's own AI agent breached Hugging Face; separate ChatGPT/Codex/API outage now resolved
stories.one_line: No update on the Hugging Face agent-breach story itself. The previously unconfirmed ChatGPT outage is now substantiated and resolved: OpenAI's status page confirmed ChatGPT/Codex/API went down together ~5am ET Monday, with a separate image-generation incident closed 8:24pm ET Monday (usage-limit-reset apology); no further anomalies as of ~12:40am ET Tuesday. Root cause undisclosed.
stories.score_note: Concrete AI-safety governance failure, not a hypothetical; reputational/regulatory risk.

stories.headline: OpenAI reportedly weighing IPO delay to 2027; Anthropic pushing toward an October 2026 debut
stories.one_line: No new IPO-timeline statement found for either company today. Both remain private; no valuation figures asserted (registry policy).

stories.headline: Bordeaux fire holds overnight but fresh heat wave forces new precautionary evacuations
stories.one_line: Gironde/Bordeaux fire (~42,000 hectares) 'stable' Tuesday morning after a calm night; ~4,000 more evacuated Tuesday from Lacanau-area campsites ahead of forecast 33-35C heat + SE wind (reignition risk, not active growth). Madrid-area fire stabilizing, one confirmed fatality unchanged since Jul 25-26; CNN's ~63,000-evacuated figure near Madrid is an updated count, not a new incident. Total France/Spain displacement still cited 300,000-360,000+.
stories.score_note: Large-scale humanitarian/disaster story; risk profile shifted from active-fire to reignition-risk.

stories.headline: Berlin Pride attack: no material change since second suspect's release
stories.one_line: Second detained suspect remains released; no new investigative developments. Euronews published a misinformation-during-the-manhunt retrospective, not a new development. Additional suspects not ruled out.
stories.score_note: International public-safety story, ongoing legal process; low direct US-market relevance. Faded from Top Stories this run.

stories.headline: Bipartisan FRONTIER Act introduced in House to regulate catastrophic-risk AI models
stories.one_line: No committee markup or hearing scheduled; coverage indicates hearings expected once the House returns from its district work period in late August.
stories.score_note: First bipartisan House frontier-AI safety bill of this scope this session; intersects with mega-cap AI-capex earnings week.

stories.headline: NDAA FY2027: House passed 216-212, stalled in Senate
stories.one_line: No further Senate floor action since the Jul 14 failed cloture vote (50-46); Thune's motion to reconsider remains pending.
stories.score_note: Direct relevance to defense/aerospace watchlist via program authorizations.

stories.headline: Federal judge blocks Minnesota prediction-market ban days before it took effect
stories.one_line: Judge Katherine Menendez (D. Minn.) issued a preliminary injunction pausing Minnesota's law criminalizing prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket), finding federal commodities law likely preempts it. Separately, in an unrelated case (KalshiEX LLC v. Williams), Judge Torres denied Kalshi's emergency injunction request the same day.
stories.score_note: Sector-relevant regulatory thread for prediction-market operators; indirect COIN/HOOD relevance via adjacent market structure.
